predecessors.name: Karamanli dynasty
predecessors.text: Tripolitania, Cyrenaica and Fezzan, over which the Ottomans 'reestablished direct control' in 1835

successors.name: Italian Africa
successors.text: Italian Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, which 'later merged into Italian Libya'

ledger.x: 1835: the Ottomans reestablish direct control of Tripolitania.
1835: the rest of the Karamanli province passes under the governor at Tripoli.
1865: the province is reclassified from an eyalet to a vilayet.
18 October 1912: the Treaty of Ouchy ends the war.
18 October 1912: the Ottomans give up Libya.

wars.name: Italo-Turkish War
wars.outcome: Italian victory: 'Italian victory' in the infobox, Italy gains the coastal areas of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica and the Dodecanese; the Treaty of Ouchy of 18 October 1912 has the Ottomans withdraw their troops and leaves a naib and a Caliph's kadi.

certainty.note: No frontier of the province is on any page: the Saharan, Fezzan and Cyrenaican limits are tribal and the Tunisian frontier is unfixed.

The Tunisian frontier is sharp: 'a border on the coast between Tunisia and Tripolitania in 1886', extended 'down to the vicinity of Ghadames in 1892', delimited by the treaty of 19 May 1910 and demarcated with pillars in 1910-11…
